changes.evidence: The initial is a long undotted upright ending in a left hook. Its full height favours J, but an undotted cursive j remains possible; the crop does not settle case.

changes.location: Heading: year on second physical line
changes.evidence: 1975 stands on a separate line immediately below the right-hand end of the place/day/month line. The two heading lines are retained.
A descending p is followed by a compact a and a short separate r shoulder before les; no cancellation crosses the word.
The low curve under the first portion of the word continues from the g descender and turns back left. There is no independent underline beneath cogitations. The letters themselves read cogitations.

changes.h: es-tu; note: es surcharge un est
changes.evidence: The live e and s precede a separately cancelled tall looped stem. Several heavy cross-strokes obscure its original crossbar and foot. A former t is the best reading, but it is not fully separable from the cancellation.

The final character has a tall doubled curl and a heavily retraced low loop. The tall component favours t, while the compressed lower curl permits s. The preceding serai is legible; grammar is not used to decide the final letter.

changes.location: Paragraph 2: boundary between conditional and tu
changes.evidence: There is blank space after the terminal curl at the end of the first line. The next line begins directly with tu, without a leading joining dash. The crop covers the first-line ending only; half a supplies the second-line beginning.

Two detached compact marks stand one above the other. The lower mark has no visible a body or connecting return stroke. Their arrangement agrees with the two dots after France; the fuller accented à forms elsewhere in this same paragraph have a separate lower letter body.
A long f stem is followed by the compact av group, a rounded o/r group, a detached i dot and a final s curl. The longer sequence and second internal syllable needed by fantaisies are not present.
The initial low n arch, round a, descending loop of g and short e/r ending can be distinguished. The long return beneath the start belongs to g.

The low leftward sweep is connected to the g descender and lies beneath only the earlier letters. No separate underline is visible; it has the same structural relation to g as the descenders in cogitations and nager.
The initial e has a short near-vertical accent stroke. The i carries one compact dot, not a two-armed circumflex; the remaining tre is legible. The absent circumflex is not supplied.

changes.location: Paragraph 3: cancelled text after constructive pour
changes.evidence: The cancellation covers two separated groups. In the first, low u/n forms and a small loop permit une. In the second, a low initial curl, two taller stems, intermediate low curves and the final re-like tail permit structure. Oblique cancelling strokes obscure substantial portions, so this is a tentative two-word reading, not a secure recovery.

After the dotted i and separately accented e, the word ends with one shallow r-like arch and a falling terminal stroke. There is no separately identifiable final e, but the ending might compress re; the crop does not settle the two alternatives.

Under the cancellation, the beginning permits évi, a tall loop survives at the d position, and the later low minims with an upright terminal permit -emment. Several joins remain obscured. The insertion bien sûr is not used to determine the cancelled spelling.
A distinct short hooked comma follows the final cancelled-word stroke and precedes le. It sits outside the cancellation, and is retained after the replacement bien sûr.

The first group is faded. A detached low vertical tail favours q and a raised mark at the right can be an apostrophe. The lost connection between tail and body leaves où followed by au possible; the raised mark could then belong to an accent. The following au is clear.

doubts.reason: Undotted long initial with a lower hook; case is not conclusively encoded.
Cancellation is certain; the underlying letter is plausibly t but partially hidden.
Tall curl and retraced bottom do not uniquely distinguish t and s.
Two groups and several surviving stems support this tentative reading; much of both words remains crossed over.
The final arch can be r alone or a compressed re; no distinct terminal e can be isolated.
Surviving letter sequence supports the word but cancellation prevents a certain complete reading.
Fading disconnects the lower tail from the first body; raised marks do not uniquely separate apostrophe from accent.

notes: The manuscript is the opening sheet of a French letter addressed to Larry, with author page number 1 and archive foliation 146. The heading gives Villecun, 17/19, an uncertain case for Juillet/juillet, and 1975 on its own line. H’s page 145 and its provenance note are editorial; its note already acknowledges author page 1 and foliation 146, so neither is counted as an H omission.

The first paragraph congratulates the addressee on his daughter’s birth. The second asks about nationality and academic status, a possible position at Montpellier, and visiting Montpellier or Villecun to discuss his favoured subjects. These are the author’s questions, not factual claims independently checked here.

The third paragraph acknowledges a response to a long letter and a constructive approach to the proposed theory. The author describes the construction of a non-strict n-category notion and its nerve functor as having the merit of existing and being a first precise approach, while criticising technicality and lack of intuition. The sheet stops at 1-cat. et with the comparison and parenthesis unfinished.

Author qualifications retained include heureusement, quelque peu, Si cela pouvait s’arranger, guère, seulement partiellement, que je prévois, certes and the inserted bien sûr. They are not reader doubt marks.
The mathematical wording n-catégorie, foncteur nerf and 1-cat. was inspected directly. No proof, calculation or mathematical consistency check was performed, and no check event is claimed.

The two clear C doubt resolutions are the colon after position and the absence of a circumflex over i in épitre. Six other C unsure loci remain explicitly uncertain. The formerly illegible cancelled material after pour is given only as the tentative two-word reading une structure.

No grammar-based repairs were made: the conditional ending remains uncertain; no hyphen was supplied across the conditional/tu line boundary; the colon after position and the possible incomplete ending premièr were retained. No definite author slip is asserted from these uncertain or context-dependent readings.

coverage: The whole image was viewed once for layout, followed sequentially by the supplied upper and lower full-resolution halves, once each. Every physical body line was read against both complete witnesses, including their agreed words, accents, abbreviations, punctuation, the heading and salutation, the author page number, both insertions, all three cancellations and the archive foliation. The lower-half overlap was used as supplied, without enlarging an entire half again. Nine tight deep crops were then made and viewed once each for the remaining unresolved places. No diagrams, drawings, displayed mathematics, marginal prose, closing or signature occur on this sheet. H did not omit a complete live prose block; its emphasis on cogitations and longue is not supported by an independent underline, its hyphen between the conditional and tu is not visible, and it omits the live comma before le flanc. The complete reading retains the cote marker, all three prose paragraphs, and the unfinished last line. No other readers, pages, outside text, OCR or web sources were consulted.
